questions.question: Which pair of annotations does @RestController combine?
questions.explanation: @RestController = @Controller + @ResponseBody, so every method writes its return value into the response body.

questions.question: A method inside a plain @Controller returns the String "home" and has no @ResponseBody. How does Spring treat that String?
options: As a view name to look up
questions.explanation: Without @ResponseBody, a returned String in a @Controller is a view name, and a view resolver tries to find that page.

questions.question: In a @RestController, @GetMapping("/hi") public String hi() { return "Hello"; } is called. What does the client receive?
options: A 404 error, because no view named Hello exists
questions.explanation: In a @RestController the returned String is the response body, so the client gets the text Hello.

questions.question: A @Controller method returns "redirect:/rooms". What does the browser get back?
options: A 302 response that sends it to /rooms
A 500 error because redirects are not supported
The JSON of the rooms with status 200 on the same request
questions.explanation: The redirect: prefix makes Spring answer 302 with a Location, and the browser then makes a new request to /rooms.

questions.question: A developer writes @Controller on a class whose method @GetMapping("/api/items") returns List<Item>. Calls to it fail instead of returning JSON. What is the fix?
options: Move the class to another package
Use @RestController, or add @ResponseBody to the method
Add the redirect: prefix to the path
questions.explanation: Without @ResponseBody the returned list is treated as a view, so the class should be a @RestController or the method needs @ResponseBody.
